changes: month normalized to Vaiśākha (written vaisāṣa), pakṣa to kṛṣṇa (vadī)
purpose reworded: the colophon is a pious wish of the scribe, not a statement of purpose
notes expanded on era and the lacuna

date.as_written: śrīsamvat 1947 sāla mītī(!) vaisāṣa(!) vadī(!)10 roja2

purpose: pious wish: mama śaṃkaraprītir astu (may Śaṅkara be pleased with me)
notes: No human names survive. The colophon says 'mama (‥)': the lacuna after 'mama' could have held the scribe's or owner's name, but nothing can be read there. The era is not named. 'samvat … sāla mītī … roja' is Nepali-style dating from the Gorkhā period, so the year is VS: 1947 − 57 = 1890 CE. Vaiśākha falls in April–May 1890. The catalogue field (SAM 1947) agrees.
